get.description: Tiles and per-day series over the last 7, 30 or 90 whole UTC days (including today). `segment` is `agents` (has at least one non-deleted agent), `people` (no agents, has issued a credential), `unclassified` (neither) or `all`. `apiCalls` counts tracked operations; `testCheqSent` is testnet CHEQ from completed faucet requests. Needs the `admin:analytics:read` scope.

Tracked operations grouped by operation, most called first (at most 100). Studio records an `operation` row for the operations it meters, not for every HTTP request. A call failed when it was unsuccessful or its `outcome` was `error`; `errorRate` is the failed share from 0 to 1. `avgMs` is 0 when no duration was recorded. An operation with no known route is returned with its name as `route` and an empty `method`. Needs the `admin:analytics:read` scope.
Customers with the most tracked operations in the range. Needs the `admin:analytics:read` scope.
Accounts per plan, and the percentage on a paid plan (plans named in `PAID_PLAN_NAMES`, default `build`). Needs the `admin:analytics:read` scope.

paidPercent.description: Share of accounts on a paid plan, 0 to 100, one decimal place.

get.description: Steps for the customers who signed up in the range. A customer counts at a step only if it reached all the steps before it. `first-credential`: signed up, funded address (completed faucet request), first DID, first credential issued. `first-agent`: signed up, funded address, first DID, registered an agent, agent card signed. `medianSecondsFromPrevious` is null for the first step or when nobody reached the step. Percent and drop are for the client to work out from `accounts`. Needs the `admin:analytics:read` scope.

get.description: Get an API key. If the API key is not provided, the latest not revoked API key it returns.

Every staff action that changed state (customer deletion, feature flag changes), newest first. Append-only. `target` is the customer id; the log never holds a customer's name or email, so an entry outlives the customer it records. `staff` is the acting staff member's Studio email where known, otherwise the actor id. Needs the `admin:audit:read` scope.

Staff search over customers, newest first. Counts only: never keys, credential contents, claim values or API keys. Needs the `admin:customers:read` scope. `status` is `active` when the customer has a tracked operation in the last 30 days and `inactive` otherwise. `plan` is the customer's plan name (`none` when it has no paid or free plan role). `usage.apiCalls30d` counts tracked operations in the last 30 days.

put.description: Creates or replaces one flag, either global or for one customer. Every change is audited.

route.description: Engine flags only. Omit to apply to every route.

delete.description: For support-triggered deletions (e.g. a customer emailing in to ask for their account to be deleted) rather than self-service. Runs the same hard-delete pipeline as `DELETE /account`: cancels any active Stripe subscription, deletes the Logto user, then deletes the customer row and everything it owns. Does not export keys on the customer's behalf and cannot remove records already written to the ledger. The target is `customerId` from the body when given, otherwise the customer named by the `customer-id` header (machine-to-machine calls). Staff cannot delete their own organisation. A customer on a paid plan also needs `confirmPaidPlan: true`. The deletion and its `adminAuditLog` row (actor, action, customer id, reason, ticket) are written in one transaction. Requires `{ "confirm": true }` and a `reason`.

customerId.description: The customer to delete. Defaults to the customer named by the `customer-id` header.

confirmPaidPlan.description: Must be true when the customer is on a paid plan.

400.description: Missing confirmation or reason, an invalid field, or a paid plan without `confirmPaidPlan`.

403.description: The caller is not staff, or is trying to delete their own organisation.

500.description: The deletion pipeline failed partway through; the response body records which steps completed.
